articles.headline: Una década de incendios en Lugo: cada vez menos fuegos, pero más graves
articles.subtitle: La provincia registra la cifra más baja de incendios de la última década, pero la superficie quemada no deja de crecer. Esta misma semana, los fuegos de Taboada, junto a la LU-611, volvieron a poner en alerta a la comarca.
articles.body:
El balance de la última década de incendios en Lugo encierra una paradoja: cada vez arde menos el monte en número de fuegos, pero la superficie quemada no deja de crecer. Los datos recogidos por El Progreso muestran que la provincia registra la cifra más baja de incendios del decenio mientras las hectáreas arrasadas alcanzan cotas cada vez más altas.

El caso de Taboada, uno de los municipios más castigados, ilustra el fenómeno: el fuego declarado a mediados de agosto muy cerca de la LU-611 obligó a movilizar a numerosos efectivos y se sumó a una ola de incendios que ha marcado el verano. La Voz de Galicia resume la paradoja: la provincia sufre menos incendios que nunca, pero se queman más hectáreas.

Detrás del cambio de patrón están la despoblación y el abandono del monte: caen los fuegos pequeños y tradicionales, pero crece la carga de combustible acumulada, lo que hace más virulentos los grandes incendios. La Xunta mantiene activos los dispositivos de prevención ante un final de verano que aún puede deparar episodios graves.

articles.headline: El PP de Lugo exige recuperar el tren-hotel nocturno con Barcelona
articles.subtitle: Los populares reclamaron en un acto en Sarria la vuelta del servicio nocturno, suprimido hace años, como reclamo turístico para la provincia y el Camino de Santiago. La formación pide a Renfe una respuesta concreta.
articles.body:
El PP de Lugo reclamó este jueves en Sarria la recuperación del tren-hotel nocturno que unía la provincia con Barcelona, un servicio suprimido hace años y que los populares consideran clave para el turismo y la conexión ferroviaria de la provincia.

Durante un acto en la villa, la formación defendió que la vuelta del servicio beneficiaría a toda la provincia y, muy especialmente, al Camino Francés, uno de los itinerarios con más peregrinos. La petición, trasladada también a Renfe, se suma a las reivindicaciones históricas por la mejora de las conexiones ferroviarias del norte de Lugo.

El tren-hotel nocturno desapareció de los horarios hace años y, desde entonces, las reclamaciones para recuperarlo se han repetido sin éxito. Los populares confían en que esta vez el Gobierno atienda una demanda que consideran mayoritaria entre los vecinos de la provincia.

articles.headline: Tercera jornada de protestas en Ceuta: cargas policiales, incendios y bloqueo de la ayuda de Cruz Roja
articles.subtitle: Los manifestantes quemaron asentamientos de migrantes en la playa del Trampolín y la Policía cargó para evitar más incidentes. Los militares piden poder hacer uso de la fuerza mientras los agentes denuncian estar 'abandonados en el caos'.
articles.body:
La crisis de Ceuta encadenó este jueves su tercera jornada de protestas, que derivaron en cargas policiales, incendios de asentamientos y el bloqueo de la ayuda de Cruz Roja en la playa del Trampolín, según 20minutos. La tensión no da tregua a una ciudad que lleva un mes en el centro de la crisis migratoria.

El polvorín social se inflama: los militares reclaman al Gobierno poder hacer uso de la fuerza y la Guardia Civil exige 'mano dura', mientras policías, guardias civiles y militares describen días 'al límite' y denuncian sentirse 'abandonados en el caos', recoge El Mundo. Europa Press informó de que la Policía cargó contra manifestantes tras quemar asentamientos de migrantes en la playa.

El Gobierno, por su parte, insiste en que no tenía 'información ni previa ni precisa' de la entrada masiva de migrantes, y el PP y los socios de la coalición reclaman más firmeza frente a Marruecos. La ciudad espera una respuesta política a la altura de una crisis que se ha instalado en sus calles.

articles.headline: Roban en cuatro minutos el Tesoro de Villena, joya de la Edad de Bronce
articles.subtitle: Los ladrones entraron por un lateral del museo y se llevaron uno de los conjuntos de orfebrería prehistórica más valiosos de Europa. La investigación apunta ya a tres encapuchados y el alcalde asegura que la ciudad está 'desolada'.
articles.body:
El Tesoro de Villena, uno de los conjuntos de orfebrería prehistórica más importantes de Europa, fue robado de madrugada en un asalto exprés que duró apenas cuatro minutos. Los asaltantes accedieron por un lateral del museo y se llevaron las piezas, datadas entre el 1300 y el 1000 antes de Cristo, según las primeras informaciones de 20minutos.

La BBC describió el robo como un golpe ejecutado en una operación relámpago, y The Guardian subrayó el valor excepcional del conjunto, descubierto en 1963 y considerado una de las cumbres de la orfebrería europea de la Edad de Bronce. Europa Press detalló que los investigadores apuntan ya a tres encapuchados.

El alcalde de Villena, visiblemente afectado, aseguró que la ciudad está 'absolutamente desolada'. La policía trabaja para localizar a los autores e impedir que las piezas salgan del país, con protocolos de alerta activados en museos y anticuarios.

articles.headline: El incendio de la Devesa obliga a evacuar El Saler y sus campings
articles.subtitle: Las llamas, declaradas en el entorno del parque natural de La Albufera, obligaron a desalojar el pueblo y los campings del municipio valenciano, así como una torre de viviendas. No se han registrado heridos.
articles.body:
Un incendio forestal declarado en la Devesa obligó este jueves a evacuar el pueblo de El Saler y los campings del municipio valenciano, uno de los pocos núcleos habitados dentro del parque natural de La Albufera. Las llamas avanzaron cerca de las viviendas y obligaron también a desalojar una torre de pisos, según 20minutos.

RTVE informó de la evacuación de vecinos y campistas, mientras Europa Press detalló que el fuego, aún activo, ha movilizado a numerosos efectivos de bomberos y medios aéreos. El Saler es un enclave especialmente sensible por su ubicación dentro del espacio natural protegido.

No se han registrado heridos, y los equipos de extinción trabajan para contener el perímetro antes de que el viento complique las labores. El incendio reabre el debate sobre la convivencia entre los núcleos urbanos y el monte mediterráneo.

articles.headline: Burnham says Irish unity poll is 'off the table' during first NI visit as PM
articles.subtitle: On his first official visit to Northern Ireland as prime minister, Andy Burnham dismissed talk of a border poll, prompting a sharp response from Sinn Féin, which accused him of ignoring the Good Friday Agreement.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham used his first official visit to Northern Ireland as prime minister to declare that a border poll on Irish unity is 'off the table', drawing an immediate rebuke from Sinn Féin. The party said the remark was unacceptable and accused the PM of disregarding the Good Friday Agreement's provisions on the constitutional question.

The Belfast Telegraph reported that the comments sparked a political row, while the BBC said the visit was intended to reset relations with the Stormont parties. Burnham also met political leaders and discussed the executive's budget crisis during the two-day trip.

Unionist leaders welcomed the remarks: DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the PM had 'put to bed' speculation about a poll. Sinn Féin, however, insisted the constitutional question cannot be ruled out by any government and vowed to keep campaigning for a referendum.

articles.headline: Parades Commissioner resigns after critical Drumcree High Court ruling
articles.subtitle: The commissioner stepped down after the High Court quashed the commission's decision on the Drumcree parade, prompting unionist calls for the board to be dismissed. The PM said confidence in the body would be restored.
articles.body:
The Parades Commissioner has resigned following a High Court ruling that criticised the commission's handling of the Drumcree parade decision. The court quashed the commission's determination on the parade, a significant setback for the body that regulates parades across Northern Ireland.

BBC News NI reported that the commissioner stepped down in the wake of the judgment, which the Belfast Telegraph described as a critical ruling for the commission. Board member Billy Gamble also resigned, the News Letter confirmed, as unionist figures demanded the entire board be sacked.

The DUP and TUV have called for the commission to be replaced, while the prime minister insisted during his visit that 'confidence will be restored' in the body. The Drumcree controversy has become one of the most delicate issues facing the new government.

articles.headline: Nepal floods: glacier collapse identified as cause as death toll nears 500
articles.subtitle: Three days after flash floods devastated the Nepal-Tibet border region, police put the death toll at 469 with around 1,300 still missing. Scientists say a collapsed glacier triggered the disaster, and a debris-clogged river risks flooding again.
articles.body:
The death toll from the catastrophic flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet border region has risen to at least 469, with around 1,300 people still missing, police said on Friday as rescue teams entered a third day of digging through mud and debris. Dozens of villages were destroyed when the wall of water hit on Tuesday.

Scientists told the BBC that a collapsed glacier most likely triggered the disaster, sending a torrent down the valley that caught residents and tourists by surprise. The Guardian's live coverage warned that a debris-clogged river remains at risk of flooding again, complicating rescue and aid operations.

Hundreds of foreign visitors, including dozens of Britons and Australians, are among the missing. Europa Press reported that aid is being rushed into the region while the Nepalese government braces for the final toll to climb further.

articles.headline: Trump claims Strait of Hormuz as US 'new territory' as Europe braces for energy crunch
articles.subtitle: The US president has declared the blocked strait a 'new US territory', a claim Iran rejects. European gas prices have doubled and storage is at its lowest in 15 years ahead of what analysts call the most critical winter since 2008.
articles.body:
President Trump has escalated his rhetoric over the Strait of Hormuz, declaring it a 'new US territory' in a social media post that included a map labelling the waterway, ABC reported. He had earlier told a rally that the US would claim the strait 'after we finish defeating Iran', according to DW.

The strait has been effectively closed since the US-Iran war began six months ago. The Guardian notes the paradox that its value as a chokehold is eroding for Tehran, while El Mundo reports European gas prices have doubled and storage sits at its lowest level in 15 years, setting up what it calls the most critical winter in a generation.

Iran's foreign ministry dismissed the annexation claim, insisting the strait 'was, is and will remain Iranian'. With no end to the war in sight, markets are pricing in prolonged disruption to Gulf energy exports as Europe heads into winter.

articles.headline: Ratko Mladić, the 'Butcher of Bosnia', dies aged 84
articles.subtitle: The Bosnian Serb general convicted of genocide over the Srebrenica massacre has died in The Hague while serving a life sentence. Survivors and officials reacted with a mix of relief and grief to the news.
articles.body:
Ratko Mladić, the Bosnian Serb military commander convicted of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes, has died aged 84. The BBC confirmed the news, first reported by Serbian state media, and the Guardian noted he died in detention in The Hague while serving a life sentence.

Mladić was found guilty of orchestrating the Srebrenica massacre of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys in 1995, Europe's worst atrocity since the Second World War, and of the siege of Sarajevo. Spanish outlet 20minutos recalled his conviction for crimes against humanity.

BBC correspondent Allan Little, who met Mladić early in the Bosnian war, described him as 'dangerously fanatical'. Bosnian survivors of the atrocities greeted the news with a mix of relief and grief, with many recalling the loved ones he took from them.

articles.headline: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'
articles.subtitle: The executive order renames the Great Lake on the US-Canada border, drawing anger from Ottawa and ridicule from critics, who see it as another escalation of the president's trade war with Canada.
articles.body:
President Trump has signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as 'Lake America', the BBC reported, in the latest escalation of his confrontation with Canada. The president said the United States was owed a lake bearing its name and hinted he might rename oceans next.

The Canadian government rejected the move, with the prime minister's office calling it a 'deliberate' provocation amid the ongoing trade war, according to Europa Press. The Guardian reported that governors of US states bordering the lake mocked the order and noted it has no effect on Canadian jurisdiction.

The order follows months of tariff battles between Washington and Ottawa, and critics see the gesture as nationalist symbolism aimed at the president's base. Observers note the rename has no legal force beyond federal paperwork, but it deepens the chill in bilateral relations.

articles.headline: Partial lunar eclipse turns the moon blood red over Europe
articles.subtitle: Skywatchers across Europe are catching a partial lunar eclipse in the early hours of Friday, with more than 90% of the lunar disc covered at maximum. In Spain it peaks around 6:12am and is safe to watch with the naked eye.
articles.body:
A partial lunar eclipse is visible across Europe and beyond in the early hours of Friday, with the moon passing through Earth's shadow and taking on a reddish 'blood moon' hue. Wired reports that more than 90% of the lunar disc will be covered at the moment of maximum eclipse.

In Spain the eclipse runs from around 4:34am to 7:52am, peaking at 6:12am, according to 20minutos, which published viewing times and the best locations. Viewers in Northern Ireland are also in line for a good show, weather permitting, the BBC reported.

Unlike a solar eclipse, a lunar eclipse is safe to watch with the naked eye, and no special filters are needed. Cloud cover is the main enemy — clear skies over the Atlantic coast and the Mediterranean offer the best views.

articles.headline: King Harald V of Norway in 'very serious' condition as health worsens
articles.subtitle: The Norwegian palace says the 89-year-old monarch's health has deteriorated significantly, and Norwegians have been laying flowers outside the royal palace in Oslo. The Crown Prince is in close contact with his father.
articles.body:
King Harald V of Norway is in a 'very serious' condition after his health deteriorated, the royal palace said on Thursday. The BBC reported that Norwegians have been laying flowers outside the royal palace in Oslo as concern grows for the 89-year-old monarch.

El Mundo reported the worsening of the king's health and noted he had been hospitalised in recent days. Europa Press said the palace described the deterioration as significant, with Crown Prince Haakon remaining in close contact with his father.

Harald, Europe's oldest reigning monarch, has faced repeated health problems in recent years but has always returned to public duties. If his condition does not improve, the Crown Prince is expected to take on further responsibilities in running the kingdom.

articles.headline: Meta settles social media harms case for up to $16.7 billion
articles.subtitle: The agreement with 51 US states and territories ends a trial over teen safety, but a buried provision stops states from ever suing Meta over children's data used to train its age-assurance model. Global regulators are watching.
articles.body:
Meta has agreed to pay up to $16.7 billion to settle the social media harms lawsuit brought by US states, ending a trial over its alleged failure to protect young users barely a week in. Wired reported that the deal also requires substantive product changes for how teens engage with its platforms.

Buried in the agreement, TechCrunch found, is a striking provision: state attorneys general have agreed 'fully, finally and forever' not to bring COPPA or similar claims over Meta's use of children's data for training and testing its age-assurance model, which must detect under-13 users within a year. The data cannot be used for ad targeting.

The Guardian notes the settlement's global implications: other governments may seek similar concessions, while separate legal action against Meta continues from Kenya to the Netherlands. An independent auditor will monitor compliance with the terms.

articles.headline: Judge rules Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic 'illegal and baseless'
articles.subtitle: A federal judge vacated the Defense Department's designation of the AI lab as a national security risk, calling it unconstitutional retaliation over a contract dispute. The Pentagon is expected to appeal the ruling.
articles.body:
A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's attempt to blacklist Anthropic, ruling that the Pentagon's designation of the AI lab as a national security 'supply-chain risk' was 'illegal and baseless', Wired reported. The 59-page ruling by US district judge Rita Lin also lifted punitive measures imposed by nine federal agencies.

The case grew out of a dispute over a $200 million Pentagon deal to use Claude in military applications, after Anthropic insisted on limits including no support for lethal autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. Defense secretary Pete Hegseth designated the company a supply-chain risk in February, prompting two lawsuits from Anthropic.

Judge Lin noted the government is even now discussing collaboration with Anthropic on its new model, Mythos, in sensitive contexts — inconsistent with treating the lab as a saboteur. The New York Times reported the ruling as a major setback for the administration, which is expected to appeal.

articles.headline: Anthropic unveils Model Hardware Standard so AI agents can run labs safely
articles.subtitle: The research preview lets AI agents operate microscopes, liquid handlers and robotic arms in parallel, cutting integration time from weeks to minutes. Partners include Genentech, Carnegie Mellon and quantum firm QuEra.
articles.body:
Anthropic has opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification that lets AI agents safely operate physical equipment in labs and factories. Developed with HHMI Janelia, MHS uses a standardised driver so devices can be discovered and controlled without bespoke integrations.

Early partners report dramatic gains: Carnegie Mellon ran dose-response experiments about three times faster, and quantum computing firm QuEra's agent recovers its laser 'lock' 99.3% of the time without human intervention. Wired describes MHS as Anthropic's plan to let agents out of the sandbox and into the physical world.

Support is being built by AWS, Danaher, Doosan Robotics, QIAGEN, Tecan, Universal Robots, Hugging Face and Raspberry Pi. Anthropic plans to open-source the standard after gathering safety evaluations from the research preview.
